A.1: Atlanta, GA had the highest order count at 78, with Milwaukee, WI on 71 and Louisville, KY on 69. The top three are fairly close, with only nine orders separating first and third place.
A.2: Large pizzas had the longest average delivery time at 34.17 minutes, followed closely by XL at 33.08. Medium averaged 27.53 minutes and Small was lowest at 21.86, giving a 12.31-minute gap between the highest and lowest size groups.
A.3: Medium pizzas made up the largest share of orders, with 429 orders or 42.73% of the total. Small pizzas were the least common at 132 orders or 13.15%.
A.4: Card was the most used payment method with 276 orders, only five ahead of UPI at 271. Wallet and Cash were also common at 208 and 202, while Hut Points and Domino's Cash were rare at 24 and 23 orders.
A.5: Medium traffic accounted for the largest share of orders at 39.64% or 398 orders. High traffic represented 32.67% and Low traffic 27.69%, so most orders occurred under Medium or High traffic conditions.
A.6: Weekday orders averaged 3.40 toppings compared with 3.27 on weekends. The difference is only 0.13 toppings per order, so the two groups are very similar.
A.7: Fort Wayne, IN and Newark, NJ had the highest average delivery duration at 50.00 minutes. Laredo, Lexington, Minneapolis and Orlando were tied next at 45.00 minutes, making the tied results important when reading the ranking.
A.8: Peak hours contained 949 orders, equal to 94.52% of the dataset, while only 55 orders or 5.48% were non-peak. Order activity is therefore heavily concentrated in the defined peak period.
A.9: Order volume is shown across 31 Month-Year points from 2024-01 to 2026-07. The highest month was 2024-08 with 86 orders, followed by 75 in 2024-09 and then 44 in 2024-10. The lowest full month was 2024-05 with 6 orders; the last point, 2026-07, contains 7 orders and only covers data through 7 July.
A.10: Average topping count increased with pizza size in this dataset. XL was highest at 4.99 toppings, followed by Large at 3.97, Medium at 2.77 and Small at 1.69.
A.11: Little Caesars had the lowest average delay at 16.62 minutes, with Domino's second at 17.02 minutes. The difference between the two lowest-delay restaurants is just 0.40 minutes.
A.12: Stuffed Crust had the longest average delivery duration at 39.52 minutes. The rest of the top five were Gluten-Free at 32.44, Cheese Burst at 32.26, Thai Chicken at 31.67 and Sicilian at 30.86 minutes.
A.13: The busiest hour was 19:00 with 328 orders. The adjacent hours were also very busy, with 312 orders at 18:00 and 306 at 20:00, showing a strong evening concentration in order volume.
A.14: Average delay rose from 15.46 minutes in Low traffic to 17.86 in Medium and 19.16 in High traffic. The High-traffic average is 3.70 minutes above the Low-traffic average.
A.15: Complexity 6 was the largest category at 30.68% of orders, followed by Complexity 12 at 22.81% and Complexity 20 at 20.12%. Together these three categories account for 73.61% of all orders, while Complexity 3 and 15 contain only two orders each.
A.16: The two performance measures identify different leaders. Papa John's had the shortest average delivery duration at 28.19 minutes, while Little Caesars had the lowest average delay at 16.62. Domino's had the longest average delivery duration at 30.26 minutes and Marco's Pizza had the highest average delay at 18.44.
A.17: Order volume reached its maximum at 19:00 with 328 orders, while average delay peaked one hour later at 20:00 with 19.97 minutes. The 21:00 delay was also high at 19.75 minutes, though that value comes from only three orders and carries much less weight than the main evening peak.
A.18: Non-Veg had the highest order volume at 216 with an average topping density of 0.760. Cheese Burst had 188 orders and the highest average density at 0.845. The supplied Topping Density field is based on toppings per kilometre, so it should be read as the provided dataset measure rather than a pure pizza-size indicator.
A.19: Traffic mix varies across payment methods. High traffic represented 44.57% of Card orders, Medium traffic was largest for Cash at 48.02% and UPI at 47.60%, while Low traffic was largest for Wallet at 44.71%. Hut Points is 95.83% High traffic, but that payment method has only 24 orders, so the percentage comes from a small base.
A.20: The dashboard brings together restaurant performance, traffic-related delay and hourly demand. Papa John's had the shortest average delivery duration at 28.19 minutes, while Marco's Pizza had the highest average delay at 18.44. High traffic produced the highest average delay at 19.16 minutes, and demand reached 328 orders at 19:00. Looking at the three views together points to evening demand and high-traffic conditions as the main areas where delivery performance deserves attention.

B.1: Atlanta, GA leads the location ranking with 78 orders. Milwaukee, WI follows with 71 and Louisville, KY with 69, so the first three locations are separated by only nine orders and there is no large gap at the top.
B.2: Large and XL pizzas form the slower-delivery pair, averaging 34.17 and 33.08 minutes respectively. Small pizzas average 21.86 minutes, which is more than eleven minutes below XL and over twelve minutes below Large.
B.3: Medium pizzas account for 42.73% of all orders, with 429 orders. Small pizzas account for 13.15% with 132 orders, so the Medium share is more than three times the Small share.
B.4: Card and UPI dominate payment activity with 276 and 271 orders. Combined they represent 547 of the 1,004 orders, while Wallet and Cash contribute 208 and 202; Hut Points and Domino's Cash remain small categories with 24 and 23.
B.5: Medium traffic is the largest group at 39.64%, followed by High at 32.67% and Low at 27.69%. Medium and High together account for 72.31% of orders, so most deliveries took place outside the Low-traffic category.
B.6: Average toppings are almost unchanged between the two day types: 3.40 on weekdays and 3.27 on weekends. A gap of 0.13 suggests day type has little practical effect on topping count in this sample.
B.7: Fort Wayne and Newark are tied at the highest average delivery duration of 50.00 minutes. The next group sits at 45.00 minutes across four locations, leaving a five-minute gap between the first tier and the next tied tier.
B.8: There are 949 Peak Hour orders compared with 55 Non-Peak Hour orders. Peak activity is therefore roughly seventeen times the non-peak count and represents 94.52% of the dataset.
B.9: Monthly volume reaches 86 orders in 2024-08 and 75 in 2024-09 before dropping to 44 in 2024-10. Across the full 31-point sequence, 2024-05 is the lowest complete month at 6 orders; 2026-07 has 7 orders but covers only the first seven days of July.
B.10: XL pizzas average 4.99 toppings, almost three times the Small average of 1.69. Large sits at 3.97 and Medium at 2.77, giving a clear step-up in topping count across the size categories.
B.11: Little Caesars and Domino's are the two lowest-delay restaurants at 16.62 and 17.02 minutes. Their averages are only 0.40 minutes apart, so both perform similarly on this measure.
B.12: Stuffed Crust stands well above the other top-five pizza types at 39.52 minutes. Gluten-Free is next at 32.44, a difference of 7.08 minutes, followed closely by Cheese Burst, Thai Chicken and Sicilian.
B.13: Demand is concentrated in the 18:00 to 20:00 window: 312 orders occur at 18:00, 328 at 19:00 and 306 at 20:00. Those three hours contain 946 orders, leaving very little volume across the remaining observed hours.
B.14: High traffic has an average delay of 19.16 minutes, compared with 17.86 for Medium and 15.46 for Low. The High-traffic average is 3.70 minutes, about 24%, above the Low-traffic average.
B.15: Complexity 6 contributes 30.68% of orders, with Complexity 12 at 22.81% and Complexity 20 at 20.12%. These three levels together make up 73.61% of the order mix, showing that the distribution is concentrated in a few complexity categories.
B.16: Restaurant rankings change depending on the measure used. Papa John's is quickest on average delivery duration at 28.19 minutes, while Little Caesars has the lowest average delay at 16.62. At the other end, Domino's records the longest average duration at 30.26 and Marco's Pizza the highest average delay at 18.44.
B.17: The demand peak and delay peak occur at different times. Orders are highest at 19:00 with 328, then average delay reaches its maximum at 20:00 with 19.97 minutes. The one-hour shift suggests the busiest period may be followed by the greatest delivery pressure; the 21:00 delay of 19.75 is based on only three orders.
B.18: The pizza type with the most orders is not the one with the highest topping density. Non-Veg leads volume with 216 orders and a density of 0.760, while Cheese Burst reaches the highest density at 0.845 with 188 orders. This separation shows that order popularity and the supplied density measure do not move together consistently.
B.19: Each payment-method row represents its own 100% traffic mix. Card has its largest share in High traffic at 44.57%; Cash and UPI lean toward Medium at 48.02% and 47.60%; Wallet leans toward Low at 44.71%. The very high High-traffic share for Hut Points should be treated carefully because that method has only 24 orders.
B.20: The three views highlight different parts of the delivery process. Restaurant results show where average speed and delay differ, the traffic view shows delay rising to 19.16 minutes under High conditions, and the hourly view shows demand peaking at 328 orders at 19:00. Taken together, the strongest operational pressure appears around the evening demand peak and under heavier traffic, while restaurant performance still varies depending on whether duration or delay is used as the benchmark.
